title: Introducing Google Cloud Modernize, transforming for (and with) AI
source_used: Google Cloud blog (Google Cloud's own post)
key_facts: Google Cloud announced Google Cloud Modernize on 5 Oct 2026: a portfolio that brings together Migration Center, Google Cloud VMware Engine, Google Cloud Mainframe Modernization and a new EKS-to-GKE Migration Agent, with what it calls agentic capabilities for infrastructure assessment, platform modernization and application modernization.

Modernization Hub is a newly launched in-console experience where developers and architects can analyze source code, map dependencies and speed up modernization for Java, .NET and mainframe applications; it integrates the App Modernization CLI (CodMod), which uses Gemini to analyze large source code repositories.

In Migration Center, the Agentic Quick Estimator (generally available) uses new Gemini capabilities to turn VMware inventory exports into total cost of ownership projections for Compute Engine; Google says this condenses weeks of spreadsheet modeling into minutes.

The EKS-to-GKE Agentic Migration (public preview) automates moving workloads from AWS Elastic Kubernetes Service to GKE (discovery, Kubernetes manifest translation, storage and network mapping) with human-in-the-loop approval gates.

New compute options: X5 (GA) with single-node 43 TiB memory for SAP S/4HANA, above the previous 29 TiB ceiling; M4N (GA), which Google says cuts licensing costs by more than 20% for Oracle and other core-licensed databases; Z4D (GA) and Z4M (preview) with large local NVMe storage and 400 Gbps networking.
Mainframe tools named: Mainframe Assessment Tool, Dual Run (replays live production transactions on both the mainframe and the new cloud applications before go-live) and Mainframe Connector.

Customer examples given by Google: NetEase Games on GKE (scaling time from hours to five minutes, server costs down 40%), Intesa Sanpaolo (Dual Run in its core banking move off the mainframe), Deutsche Börse Group (SAP S/4HANA and DAX calculations; disaster recovery from hours to minutes, aggregation latency down over 50%).
Google offers a no-cost modernization assessment through its Rapid Migration & Modernization Program (RaMP) and a webinar on 17 November; Cognizant is named as a delivery partner.
quote_evidence: Today, we’re announcing Google Cloud Modernize, an end-to-end transformation portfolio to help enterprises collapse multi-year roadmaps with the power of AI.

Central to this portfolio is Modernization Hub, a newly launched in-console experience where developers and architects can analyze source code, map dependencies, and accelerate modernization for Java, .NET, and mainframe applications.
This condenses weeks of spreadsheet modeling into a defensible business case in minutes.
why_it_matters_hint: Gives developers and IT teams at large companies AI help to examine and move older Java, .NET, mainframe and Amazon-hosted Kubernetes systems onto Google Cloud; Google says it cuts weeks of cost modeling to minutes.
event_date: 5 Oct 2026 (post says 'Today, we're announcing'; Google Cloud's blog feed lists it at 16:00 UTC on 5 Oct 2026)
notes: Read in full from fulltext/C03-02.txt; date confirmed from Google Cloud's own blog feed, inside the window. A vendor launch post: every performance or savings figure (20% licensing cut, 40% server cost cut, weeks to minutes, 50% latency cut) is Google's or its quoted customers', with no independent test. Part of the package is a bundle of existing tools; the post marks the EKS-to-GKE agent and Z4M as preview. Our reading: the customer examples show Google Cloud products already in use, not tests of the new package. Cognizant quote is marketing text and not used.
